blocks.text: The doctor’s question echoed in the room.
My newborn son lay against my chest, wrapped tightly in a white hospital blanket. His tiny fingers curled around mine.
But the doctor looked as if he had just seen a ghost.
“That Julian Vance is the biological father.”
“Please bring me the newborn identification file.”
“My name is Dr. Adrian Cole,” he said quietly. “And I need to explain something before I tell you what I think is happening.”
“Your son has a very distinctive birthmark.”
A small, reddish-brown crescent-shaped mark sat just below my son’s left collarbone.
The doctor’s eyes filled with tears again.
Three months earlier, my life had been completely different.
Julian and I had been married for six years.
We weren’t rich, but we had a comfortable home, steady jobs, and what I believed was a happy marriage.
Then, one Tuesday evening, Julian placed divorce papers on our dining table.
I laughed because I genuinely thought he was joking.
He refused to attend doctor’s appointments.
And when I asked him whether he wanted to know the baby’s sex, he replied:
And every night, I whispered to my unborn son that no matter what happened, I would never abandon him.
I woke before sunrise with contractions.
And less than ten minutes after that, Dr. Cole told me something that turned everything upside down.
I saw my son’s newborn identification number.
Underneath it was a handwritten notation:
Distinctive congenital marking: crescent-shaped birthmark, left clavicle.
“My wife and I had a baby girl fourteen years ago.”
Then I saw the photograph attached to it.
The exact same crescent-shaped birthmark.
“They found something in your son’s preliminary genetic screening.”
“The sample matches a stored genetic profile from fourteen years ago.”
“Did Julian ever tell you he had a sister?”
Then he revealed the name written beneath the picture.
But according to the hospital records, Lillian had died fourteen years earlier.
Dr. Cole explained that fourteen years ago, his newborn daughter had been declared dead after complications during delivery.
His wife had never recovered emotionally.
But several years later, Dr. Cole discovered irregularities in the hospital records.
The newborn’s identification bracelet had disappeared.
He had spent years trying to discover what happened.
And now, his laboratory had found a genetic connection between that missing infant and my newborn son.
Julian wasn’t just the father of my son.
He was the brother of Dr. Cole’s missing daughter.
But that still didn’t explain why my baby matched her genetic profile.
“Your son inherited the same rare genetic marker from Julian.”
He reached into the folder and pulled out one final document.
“Julian isn’t your son’s biological father.”
“The DNA comparison came back yesterday.”
Suddenly, every strange thing Julian had done during my pregnancy made sense.
He hadn’t simply decided he didn’t care.
Dr. Cole placed another document in front of me.
Then I saw the name of the woman listed as the child’s biological mother.
“Julian wasn’t born into the Vance family either.”
“Fourteen years ago, my daughter disappeared. Around the same time, a newborn boy appeared in another hospital under suspicious circumstances.”
“Julian was the baby who replaced my missing daughter.”
The man I had married had spent his entire life believing he was a Vance.
And somehow, the missing pieces of that old crime had finally led to my newborn son.
Then Dr. Cole said the sentence that shattered everything.
“Your son isn’t biologically related to Julian.”
The doctor slowly opened the final envelope.
Fourteen years ago, Dr. Cole’s daughter had disappeared.
And somehow, before her disappearance, she had given birth to a child.
Which meant Julian’s sudden divorce wasn’t about falling out of love.
